newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco Chuquicamata sees 96 output 631,170 T.
newsitem.headline: Codelco Chuquicamata sees 96 output 631,170 T.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco's huge Chuquicamata division expects its 1996 copper production to rise to 631,170 tonnes from 610,150 tonnes in 1995, reported the division's magazine Oasis.
The magazine, quoting general manager Nelson Pizarro, said the mine aims to boost copper output to 640,000 tonnes this year despite sliding mineral ore grades.
"This is really a challenge as we are committing ourselves (to increase output) although with the certainty that we will have a lower head grade," said Pizarro.
Ore grades at the pit, which has been in operation since early this century, are expected to fall from 1.07 percent last year to 1.04 percent this year.

Although the mine made up for production lost in a 10 day strike in May, the division has figures showing that every four days either a worker is injured or there is some interruption of production, he said.
"So our mission is to improve...as what is really important is to keep the continuity of the processes," said Pizarro.
One unit at the mine which failed to reach its target was the oxides division which produced 144,292 tonnes last year against a goal of 152,720 tonnes.
The shortfall was due to the strike and technical problems with the division's mineral crusher, said the magazine.
Despite the problems, the division has raised its production target this year to 157,811 tonnes, it said.
